concerns.text: The plan proposes paired t‑tests on per‑episode binary success outcomes. A paired t‑test assumes normally‑distributed differences, which is violated for binary data; a McNemar or exact binomial test would be more appropriate.
The three chosen descriptors (variance, lag‑1 autocorrelation, spectral density) are asserted to capture “latent complexity” without justification or citation, raising construct‑validity concerns.

No power analysis or sample‑size justification is provided for the N = 500 training clips and M = 200 test clips; it is unclear whether this size can reliably detect the target correlation (|r| > 0.5) or a 5 % success‑rate lift.

Deterministic tie‑breaking (always choose the lowest τ) may bias the label distribution and introduce a confound between τ and the descriptor‑based regressor, potentially inflating apparent predictive performance.
The baseline for MSE comparison predicts only the global mean τ, ignoring k; this creates an uneven baseline that may overstate the regressor’s improvement.

The plan does not explicitly control for possible confounds such as differing task‑complexity distributions between training and novel configurations, which could drive observed performance differences rather than the predicted hyperparameters.
